title: Modular SDK patterns for resumable streaming, burst retries, and cross-language sample apps
text:
Modular SDK patterns for resumable streaming, burst retries, and cross-language sample apps

description:
Deliver a set of cross-language starter templates and cookbook snippets demonstrating: resumable streaming clients, coordinated idempotent retries under bursty load, backpressure-friendly AsyncIterator patterns, and minimal server implementations (Next.js edge, FastAPI streaming endpoint, Go HTTP server). The goal is to provide pragmatic reference implementations engineering teams can copy into product repos and a short narrative explaining trade-offs (latency vs. memory, client checkpointing vs. server checkpoints).

tasks:
Design resumable streaming protocol sketch (client checkpoints + server-ack offsets)
Implement TypeScript client utilities: AsyncIterator wrapper, resume token helper, exponential backoff + jitter for chunk retries
Implement Python SDK streaming helper: generator-based resume API, context-aware cancellation, socket-level keepalive note
Implement Go example server and client showing context cancellation and idempotency tokens
Create Next.js sample that consumes a streaming endpoint and gracefully resumes after transient disconnections
Add FastAPI server example that exposes a /stream-checkpoint endpoint and emits offset metadata
Write CLI examples (Go and Python) demonstrating long-running streaming with local checkpoint file and resume command
Add README/cookbook explaining patterns, recommended defaults, and metrics to watch (retries, resumed sessions, duplicate-ids)

acceptance_criteria:
TS/JS example includes an AsyncIterator that can resume after an interrupted stream with a provided resume token
Python SDK helper exposes `stream_with_resume(prompt, resume_token=None)` with docs and tests
Go example demonstrates graceful cancellation when parent context is cancelled and retains idempotency tokens for retry safety
All samples include small benchmarks/notes about memory and latency trade-offs and suggested defaults for production
PRs linked to sample repos with at least 1 engineering review and automated smoke tests for basic resume flow

implementation_notes:
Prefer zero-dependency snippets that can be copy-pasted; provide optional subdir for production-ready implementations that import SDK helpers. For web sample, show both fetch streaming and WebSocket fallback. Include small utility to compute conservative rewind length (default 8 tokens).

notes:
Key trade-offs documented: (1) Client-first checkpointing reduces server state but shifts responsibility to clients; (2) Conservative rewind on resume prevents missing tokens but may surface small duplicates; (3) Backpressure in browsers implemented via async iterator pause/resume is preferred over large in-memory buffering

code_examples:
TypeScript: AsyncIterator resume pattern with ExponentialBackoff and resume token helper
Python: generator-based stream_with_resume(prompt, resume_token=None) that yields partial chunks and persists checkpoint file
Go: context-aware client and server example with idempotency-token header and offset metadata
CLI: python resume_cli.py --checkpoint /tmp/stream.ckpt and go resume-cli --checkpoint-file /var/tmp/stream.json

comments:
2026-03-03 - Luis Chen: Spike showed that resume tokens should include both sequence offset and a short hash of the prompt to avoid miss-resumes when model prompt changes.
2026-03-05 - Anika Verma: Decided to prefer client-side checkpoint files for CLI and browser localStorage for web samples; server-side checkpoints add complexity for little value in our target use cases.
2026-03-07 - Priya Natarajan (review): Requested clearer guidance about duplicate token consumption and how to surface duplicate detection metrics in Console; added acceptance criterion to document metrics.
2026-03-09 - EngInfra (feedback): Recommending small JSON checkpoint with resume_token, model_version, and offset to keep compatibility with future runtime changes.
2026-03-11 - Luis Chen: Implemented TS helper and basic Next.js demo; observed ~3% extra token duplication on resume in local test — added note in README about conservative offset rewind (n tokens) to avoid missing content.
